subagent_reports.topic: Design validation — prose-only native-edit recovery guidance for opencode-morph-fast-apply

sources.label: OpenCode official plugins docs (tool.execute.before intercepts args; throw to block)
sources.summary: tool.execute.before receives output.args and can mutate args or throw to block a tool BEFORE it runs (e.g. reject .env reads, escape bash commands). No documented contract to observe a native tool's failure and substitute a retry or reroute.

sources.label: OpenCode-Book 13.2 Plugin Lifecycle Hooks — exact hook signatures
sources.summary: tool.execute.before(input,{args})=>Promise<void> modifies input args only; tool.execute.after(input,{title,output,metadata})=>Promise<void> modifies display output only. Both return void. No failure signal, no pass/fail branch, no re-invocation path. Confirms plugin cannot intercept/retry a native tool failure.

sources.label: OpenCode issue #31680 — before-hook arg mutation was a no-op
sources.summary: Upstream bug: tool.execute.before arg mutation historically had no effect because the executor read original args, not hook output. Demonstrates the interception surface is fragile and unsuitable as a reliable native-edit retry/reroute substrate.

sources.label: Local: index.ts morph_edit tool description + tool.execute.after hook
sources.summary: Embedded morph_edit description already carries WHEN-TO-USE routing and a Morph-API-failure/timeout -> native edit FALLBACK line (L273). The only execution hook used is tool.execute.after for TUI title branding (L330) — display only, consistent with docs.

sources.label: Local: instructions/morph-tools.md always-on routing policy
sources.summary: Canonical always-on instruction with First-Action table and Fallback Policy. Currently covers initial selection and Morph->native fallback only; has no post-native-edit-failure recovery branch — the exact gap the design fills.

sources.label: Local: index.test.ts drift tests read all owned surfaces
sources.summary: Tests already readFileSync both instructions/morph-tools.md and README.md and assert prose content; the pattern extends cleanly to assert the recovery rule across all three surfaces (index.ts description, instruction, README), satisfying SC4/AC5 and DONT4.

sources.label: Local: prior archived change captured the same ownership boundary
sources.summary: Prior research already recorded that plugin docs establish tool.execute.before argument interception but NOT a native-tool failure rewrite/retry contract — corroborating the boundary independently across two research passes.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The design adds a single, ordered, prose-only native-edit recovery policy (re-read -> at most one corrected native edit only if still small/exact -> otherwise morph_edit) to three plugin-owned routing surfaces (index.ts tool description, instructions/morph-tools.md, README.md), preserves the existing Morph-API-failure/timeout -> native-edit fallback, and locks all three surfaces with drift tests. I independently verified the OpenCode plugin hook contract against two authoritative docs and one upstream issue. The hook surface is decisive: tool.execute.before can only mutate/throw on ARGS before a tool runs and tool.execute.after can only rewrite DISPLAY output after it runs; both return Promise<void> with no failure signal and no re-invocation capability. Therefore a plugin CANNOT observe a native edit's exact-match failure and automatically retry it or reroute to morph_edit. Automatic interception/retry is not supported by the platform. Prose-only guidance targeting the agent's own next action is the correct, and only, supported mechanism — this is the boring, proven solution (documentation + regression tests) over a novel unsupported runtime interception loop. Scope is correctly bounded: it does not touch native edit, the Morph API contract, safety guards, path confinement, secret scrubbing, readonly protections, or adv-engineer config. The design is internally consistent with the approved contract (SC1-SC5, AC1-AC5, C1-C4, DONT1-DONT4). Minor non-blocking execution risk: the plugin CANNOT structurally enforce 'at most one corrected native edit' (that bound is agent-behavioral, not machine-checkable), and tests can only assert prose PRESENCE/consistency, not runtime adherence — but this is inherent to any prose-routing change and the design already discloses it via C1 (must not claim automatic interception).

validation.notes: Design ownership boundary is source-confirmed: OpenCode plugin hooks cannot intercept/retry a native tool failure; prose-only guidance is the correct mechanism. Constraint C1 (do not claim automatic interception) is directly supported by the verified hook contract. Recommend two non-blocking planning notes: (1) keep the bounded-retry limit framed as agent-directed guidance, not a plugin-enforced guarantee, to stay truthful per C1/P33; (2) ensure drift tests assert the recovery rule in all THREE surfaces (index.ts description string, instruction file, README) so DONT4 cannot regress to single-surface coverage.

tradeoffs: Prose-only guidance is not machine-enforceable: the 'at most one corrected native edit' bound and 'do not repeat unchanged input' rule depend on agent adherence; tests can assert prose presence/consistency but not runtime behavior.
Three parallel surfaces (tool description in index.ts, instruction file, README) create a small ongoing drift-maintenance cost, mitigated by the regression tests the design mandates.

Choosing documentation over runtime interception forgoes any automatic recovery, but the platform does not support automatic native-edit failure interception, so the alternative is illusory rather than a real lost capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Automatic interception/retry of native edit failures via tool.execute.before/after
alternatives_considered.rationale: Verified against OpenCode plugin docs and OpenCode-Book 13.2: before-hook controls ARGS only (mutate/throw pre-execution), after-hook controls DISPLAY output only; both return Promise<void> with no failure signal and no re-invocation path. Issue #31680 shows the interception surface was even historically a no-op. Automatic native-edit failure retry/reroute is not a supported contract.

alternatives_considered.option: New plugin tool surface or runtime retry loop wrapping edits
alternatives_considered.rationale: Explicitly excluded by DONT2; would require the plugin to own native edit execution, which it does not. Adds an unsupported, higher-risk runtime path for zero platform-backed benefit.

alternatives_considered.option: Single-surface guidance (only the tool description, or only the instruction file)
alternatives_considered.rationale: The three surfaces are consumed independently (embedded description is always present; instruction file is opt-in always-on; README is human-facing). Single-surface guidance leaves the others silent/contradictory and violates DONT4 and SC1's cross-surface consistency requirement.

alternatives_considered.option: Prose-only aligned recovery guidance across all three surfaces + drift tests (chosen)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Only platform-supported mechanism; boring/proven (docs + regression tests); bounded scope; preserves existing Morph->native fallback; consistent with C1 truthfulness constraint and existing index.test.ts test pattern.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to design-gate completion. Implement the ordered recovery policy as prose in all three owned surfaces, keep it framed as agent-directed guidance (never as plugin-enforced interception, per C1), preserve the existing Morph-API-failure/timeout -> native-edit fallback verbatim to satisfy AC4/DONT3, and add drift tests that assert the recovery rule in each of the three surfaces (index.ts description string, instruction file, README) to satisfy SC4/AC5/DONT4.

subagent_reports.recommendation: PASS design validation. The design's central architectural claim — that this plugin cannot automatically intercept/retry native edit failures and must therefore use aligned prose-only routing guidance — is confirmed by authoritative OpenCode plugin hook documentation (before=args-only, after=display-only, both Promise<void>) and by an upstream bug showing the interception surface is fragile. This is the boring, correct solution. No blockers. Two non-blocking planning notes: (1) keep the bounded native-retry limit framed as agent guidance, not a machine-enforced guarantee, to remain truthful under C1; (2) ensure the drift tests cover all three surfaces so DONT4 cannot silently regress.

Planning: verify the new wording does not weaken the existing Morph-API-failure/timeout -> native edit FALLBACK line in index.ts (L273) per AC4/DONT3.

sources.label: Bun install/CI docs (bun ci = frozen lockfile)
sources.summary: bun ci is a real command equal to `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; installs exact versions from bun.lock and FAILS the build if package.json is out of sync with bun.lock. Requires bun.lock committed. Confirms release.yml line 22 `bun ci` is valid.

sources.label: Bun git-dependency docs (commit-ish pinning)
sources.summary: github:user/repo without a commit-ish resolves the latest commit on the default branch; a #v1.10.2 tag suffix pins a specific tag. Confirms deterministic-deploy design requires the #v1.10.2 pin.

sources.label: Bun re-resolution / lockfile reset docs

sources.label: Canonical tag-after-merge practice
sources.summary: By-the-book consensus: tag stable code on the default branch, never feature/PR branches (tag drift on rebase/force-push, branch deletion, tag points to non-released commit). Matches design's tag-only-after-merge-proof ordering.

sources.label: Tag reachability from default branch (git describe / merge-base)
sources.summary: A tag is only reachable from the default branch once its commit is merged there; git merge-base --is-ancestor / git branch --contains are the canonical reachability checks. Supports AC5 default-branch reachability proof gate.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The expanded design is architecturally sound and follows by-the-book release/deployment sequencing. Source-authored release-prep (version + CHANGELOG + test expectations) committed on the change branch, ADV archive merging to the default branch, tag-only-after-merge-proof, tag-triggered GitHub Actions release, then a separate deterministic local-deploy step (pin existing git dependency to #v1.10.2, install, sync stable instruction, backup non-secret config, verify installed version + `opencode debug config`, require restart) is the correct shape. Two integrity gaps and several ordering hazards must be respected during execution: (1) release.yml `bun ci` is frozen-lockfile install and FAILS if package.json is out of sync with the tracked bun.lock — a version bump to 1.10.2 changes package.json, so bun.lock must be regenerated/synced in the SAME release-prep commit or CI will fail on the tag. (2) CHANGELOG.md currently has no `## [1.10.2]` section (only empty Unreleased + 1.10.1); the awk extractor emits empty release notes unless a non-empty 1.10.2 section is authored first (agreement SC5/AC-changelog already requires this). (3) Local deploy pins an UNPINNED github: dependency with no lockfile in ~/.config/opencode; git-tag pins can be served from Bun's cache, so re-resolution should be forced (explicit #v1.10.2 in package.json + install; if the installed version does not read 1.10.2, clear node_modules and reinstall) and verified by reading the installed manifest version, not assumed. (4) Config-integrity ordering: backup non-secret config state BEFORE editing ~/.config/opencode/package.json (constraint C6), and treat stable-instruction sync as mandatory co-equal with the package pin (avoidance A5 — do not update the package while leaving the instruction stale). None of these compromise the accepted policy-only Morph-recovery contract; they are release-mechanics correctness requirements the agreement already largely encodes.

validation.notes: No architecture blocker and no contract-compromise risk. Design ordering (source prep -> merge -> merge-proof -> tag -> verify GH release -> pin/install/sync/backup/verify/restart) is canonical. Execution must honor four non-blocking integrity requirements captured in the assessment: (1) sync bun.lock in the version-bump commit so `bun ci` passes on the tag; (2) author a non-empty `## [1.10.2]` CHANGELOG section before tagging; (3) force + verify git-tag re-resolution on local deploy (no lockfile present, cache hazard); (4) backup-before-edit and mandatory stable-instruction sync. These are already reflected in agreement SC4/SC5/SC6/SC8, C5/C6, and A4/A5 — recommend the planning gate turn each into an explicit verification task rather than leaving them implicit.

tradeoffs: Tag-after-merge-proof adds a serialization point (cannot tag until ADV Phase 9 proves default-branch reachability) but eliminates tag-drift/orphan-tag failure modes from feature-branch tagging.
Frozen-lockfile CI (`bun ci`) buys reproducible releases but converts any package.json/bun.lock skew into a hard tag-time CI failure, so the version bump must carry the lockfile update atomically.
Pinning the local git dependency to #v1.10.2 gains determinism but loses auto-tracking of future default-branch commits; acceptable and intended for a verified deployment, and reversible.

CHANGELOG-driven release notes keep a single source of truth but make an empty/missing `## [1.10.2]` section silently produce empty GitHub release notes — a content precondition, not an error the workflow surfaces.

alternatives_considered.option: Tag the change branch / tag before merge
alternatives_considered.rationale: Canonical guidance (softwareengineering.stackexchange 442334, gitflow) says tags belong on stable default-branch commits; feature-branch tags drift on rebase/force-push and can point to never-released commits. Design already forbids this (avoidance A4, constraint C5).
release.yml runs `bun ci` = frozen-lockfile; a package.json version change with a stale bun.lock fails the tag build. Lockfile must be synced in the same release-prep commit.

alternatives_considered.option: Leave global dependency unpinned (github:JRedeker/... default branch)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Unpinned github: resolves latest default-branch commit, which is non-deterministic and defeats 'deploy exactly v1.10.2'. Pin to #v1.10.2 (Bun git commit-ish docs).

alternatives_considered.option: Publish to npm as the deployment channel
alternatives_considered.rationale: Out of scope by explicit agreement constraint C4; local OpenCode consumes the plugin via the git dependency, so a git-tag deploy is the correct and sufficient channel.

alternatives_considered.option: Update installed package only, skip stable-instruction sync
alternatives_considered.rationale: Global config loads the always-on instruction independently of the installed plugin; skipping the sync leaves policy drift (avoidance A5). Sync + verify both surfaces.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed. At planning, materialize four explicit verification tasks: (1) version bump + bun.lock sync in one commit, asserted by a local `bun ci` before tagging; (2) author non-empty `## [1.10.2]` CHANGELOG section and assert awk-extract is non-empty; (3) local deploy = backup non-secret config -> pin #v1.10.2 -> install -> if installed manifest version != 1.10.2 force clean reinstall (rm node_modules) -> read installed version + sync stable instruction + `opencode debug config` exit 0; (4) gate tag push on ADV Phase 9 default-branch reachability proof and confirm `gh release view v1.10.2` non-draft with notes.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Validation PASS, high confidence, low risk, no contract compromise. Design ordering is canonical (tag only after merge-proof; deterministic #v1.10.2 pin; verify-not-assume deploy). Before/at planning, convert four implicit integrity requirements into explicit tasks: (a) sync bun.lock in the version-bump commit so tag-time `bun ci` passes; (b) add a non-empty `## [1.10.2]` CHANGELOG section so the awk extractor emits real release notes; (c) force + verify git-tag re-resolution on local deploy since ~/.config/opencode has no lockfile and Bun may serve a cached git ref (assert installed manifest reads 1.10.2, clean-reinstall if not); (d) backup non-secret config BEFORE editing package.json and treat stable-instruction sync as mandatory co-equal with the package pin.
follow_ups: Confirm ~/.config/opencode/package.json edit will preserve the two unrelated deps (@opencode-ai/plugin pin, opencode-firecrawl) — only the morph line gets #v1.10.2.

During local deploy, verify installed version by reading the installed node_modules manifest, not by assuming bun add succeeded, because a cached git ref can leave an older commit in place with no lockfile to enforce the pin.

sources.label: PyPA gh-action-pypi-publish Discussion #42 (release-PR tag ownership)
sources.summary: Authoritative description of the exact tension in this design: a tag on a release/feature branch 'does not belong to main and can easily be deleted'; only after the PR merges does the tag 'start belonging to main'. Confirms feature-branch tag publication is the risk being avoided.

Fix = hard-sync to origin default, confirm HEAD is squashed commit, add `git merge-base --is-ancestor` reachability gate before pushing the tag. Mirrors this design's Phase-9-merge-proof-then-tag-then-verify ordering.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The corrected design boundary is architecturally sound and matches canonical release-engineering practice. The core split — (1) source release preparation (package.json version, README pinned example, index.test.ts version/changelog assertions, non-empty CHANGELOG `## [1.10.2]` section, frozen-lockfile-clean bun.lock) is acceptance-scoped and completable pre-merge; (2) annotated tag creation, tag-triggered GitHub release publication/verification, and local deployment are mandatory post-Phase-9 operations gated on default-branch merge proof — is exactly the ordering that authoritative sources prescribe. The design correctly recognizes that tag/release CANNOT be truthful acceptance criteria for pre-merge work, because a tag pushed before merge would publish an unmerged feature-branch commit (llmbestpractices: tags point to commits on main; PyPA #42: a pre-merge tag 'does not belong to main'). The flipt-io/flipt fix (acda1ab) is a production precedent for this exact orphan-tag hazard under squash-merge and validates the design's step 5 reachability verification (tag target must equal the merged default-branch commit) as the correct structural gate rather than a heuristic. The design's failure-handling table ('Phase 9 merge unavailable → do not tag, publish, or deploy') and its rejected alternative ('Tag before merge: can publish unmerged code') are both correct and directly supported. The deployment half (pin global dependency to `github:...#v1.10.2`, verify installed manifest == 1.10.2, sync stable instruction path, report restart requirement) is deterministic and matches the design's own prior researcher-confirmed pinning rationale; unpinned default-branch resolution cannot prove deployed version, so pinning is the correct choice. Boundary preserves the user-requested end state: source metadata shipped and verifiable pre-merge, and tag/GitHub-release/local-deploy all completed after merge proof — nothing dropped, only re-sequenced to be truthful.

validation.notes: Design boundary validated against 5 authoritative external sources plus 3 in-repo workflow/manifest verifications. No blockers. The typed acceptance contract correctly scopes only pre-merge source release preparation; tag/GitHub-release/deploy are correctly reframed as post-Phase-9 mandatory completion operations gated on default-branch merge proof. This avoids feature-branch publication (the stated risk) and preserves the user-requested full end state. Two non-blocking follow-ups noted.

tradeoffs: Splitting the deliverable across the Phase-9 boundary means the ADV acceptance gate cannot mechanically prove the shipped GitHub release or local deployment; those must be verified by explicit post-archive completion evidence (tag reachability, `gh release view v1.10.2`, installed manifest version). This is the correct tradeoff — mechanical acceptance of a not-yet-mergeable artifact would be a false claim — but it shifts release-completion proof from the contract review matrix to post-archive operational evidence.

Annotated-tag-after-merge ordering adds one manual/ordered step (create+push tag at the merged commit, then verify target) versus a single pre-merge tag, in exchange for eliminating the orphan-tag/unmerged-publication failure mode. Worthwhile: the failure mode is silent and produces spanning/incorrect release notes (flipt precedent).

Pinning the global OpenCode dependency to an immutable tag ref (`#v1.10.2`) trades auto-tracking of future default-branch changes for deterministic, provable deployed version — required to satisfy the 'verify deployed manifest == 1.10.2' condition.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep tag/GitHub-release/deploy as typed acceptance criteria (pre-merge)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Cannot be truthfully satisfied before Phase 9: tagging a pre-merge feature-branch commit publishes unmerged code and orphans the tag off the default branch (PyPA #42; flipt acda1ab; llmbestpractices). Making unsatisfiable-until-merge conditions into acceptance criteria is a contract-compromise, which is exactly why discovery was re-entered.

alternatives_considered.option: Tag the local release-branch commit, then merge
alternatives_considered.rationale: Orphan-tag hazard: under squash-merge the merged commit has a new SHA, so the tag is not an ancestor of the default branch and the tag-triggered release runs against an unmerged commit. flipt-io/flipt fixed this exact bug by adding a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` reachability gate before pushing.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the global OpenCode dependency unpinned (default-branch ref)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Cannot prove which version is deployed locally; violates the design's deterministic-deployment and 'verify installed manifest == 1.10.2' requirement. git-scm confirms only pinned refs give a stable reference point.
Outside the repository's tag-triggered GitHub-release workflow and outside the agreement scope; the install path is a GitHub dependency ref, not an npm registry package.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with the corrected boundary unchanged. It is canonically correct and low-risk. Recommend the design/plan additionally encode an explicit reachability gate in the post-Phase-9 tag step — verify `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag-commit> origin/trunk` (or confirm the tag target SHA equals the merged default-branch HEAD) BEFORE pushing the tag, not only after — to structurally prevent the orphan-tag failure mode rather than detect it post-hoc (flipt precedent). Also confirm during planning that the release workflow's `bun ci` (frozen lockfile) will pass at the tagged commit by ensuring any bun.lock regeneration is committed in the acceptance-scoped source-prep step.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Design boundary is VALID — approve as-is. Acceptance contract correctly limited to pre-merge source release preparation; tag creation, GitHub release verification, and local deployment are correctly mandatory post-Phase-9 operations gated on default-branch merge proof. This avoids feature-branch publication and preserves the full user-requested end state. Add an explicit pre-push `git merge-base --is-ancestor` reachability gate to the tag step to structurally enforce (not just verify) that the tag targets the merged default-branch commit.
follow_ups: Planning: encode a pre-push reachability gate (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag-commit> origin/<default>`) in the post-Phase-9 tag step, mirroring flipt-io/flipt acda1ab, to prevent orphan tags structurally.

Planning: ensure any bun.lock regeneration triggered by the version bump is committed within the acceptance-scoped source-prep step so the tag-triggered release workflow's frozen-lockfile `bun ci` passes at the tagged commit.

Note: the briefing packet (_briefingPacket) was truncated by output budget; validation relied on the authoritative _design and _agreement artifacts plus direct in-worktree workflow/manifest reads, which were sufficient for this design-boundary question.

documents.proposal:
# Proposal: Improve Morph recovery and release it

## Problem

Native exact-string edits often fail when target text is stale or ambiguous. The plugin already provides Morph for contextual edits but lacked a clear recovery route after native `edit` failure. The implemented policy/test change is accepted; the user additionally requires it to ship as a verified local OpenCode deployment and a GitHub release.

## Direction

1. Keep the accepted policy-only Morph recovery implementation.
2. Prepare a patch release, `v1.10.2`, with source version, documentation pin, test expectation, and changelog aligned.
3. Archive only after the release-preparation commit is merged to the default branch.
4. After merge proof, push `v1.10.2`; the existing tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow creates the release from `CHANGELOG.md`.
5. Deploy the released tag locally through the configured Git dependency, then synchronize the separate configured stable instruction path and verify both installed content and effective OpenCode configuration.

## Scope

### In scope

- Existing native-edit recovery guidance and its cross-surface tests.
- `package.json`, README version example, version assertions, `CHANGELOG.md`, and tracked `bun.lock` release metadata.
- Post-merge tag/release verification for `v1.10.2`.
- Deterministic local install of the released Git tag, stable-instruction synchronization, config backup, and verification.

### Out of scope

- OpenCode native `edit` implementation.
- Morph API/runtime/safety behavior and Advance configuration.

documents.problemStatement: Host-wide OpenCode message-log analysis found 224 failed native exact-edit calls across 385 adv-engineer sessions. The dominant error is an exact-string mismatch, including “Could not find oldString in the file. It must match exactly, including whitespace, indentation, and line endings.” The current Morph plugin already exposes `morph_edit` and ships routing guidance, but that guidance has no explicit recovery path for a failed native `edit` call. The Morph plugin cannot automatically rerun or replace OpenCode’s native edit tool; the owned fix must make recovery guidance clear, consistent, and test-protected wherever this plugin communicates tool choice.

# Agreement: Improve Morph recovery and ship v1.10.2

## Objectives

1. Preserve the accepted native-edit recovery policy: re-read target content, never repeat unchanged failed input, make at most one corrected native exact edit only when still small/exact, otherwise use Morph for contextual repair.
2. Keep policy wording and regression coverage aligned across the embedded tool description, packaged always-on instruction, and README.
3. Prepare patch release `v1.10.2` source metadata and changelog notes that satisfy the tag-release workflow.
4. Complete tag publication, GitHub release verification, and deterministic local deployment only after ADV Phase 9 proves default-branch merge.

## Success Criteria

1. `index.ts`, `instructions/morph-tools.md`, and `README.md` state the bounded native-edit recovery policy.
2. `write` remains limited to new-file or intentional full-file replacement work; the existing Morph API-error/timeout → native-edit fallback remains documented.
3. Tests fail if any owned policy surface omits required recovery anchors; `bun run ci` exits 0.
4. Source package version, README pinned-version example, version assertions, and release metadata all identify `1.10.2` / `v1.10.2` consistently.
5. `CHANGELOG.md` has a non-empty `## [1.10.2]` section so the tag-release workflow can create release notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given native `edit` reports unmatched or ambiguous target, all three owned policy surfaces tell the agent to re-read and not repeat unchanged input.
2. Given re-read content leaves a small exact edit, all three surfaces permit at most one corrected native edit; otherwise they direct Morph for multi-line, scattered, whitespace-sensitive, or broader-anchoring repair.
3. Existing Morph API-error/timeout fallback and `write` boundary remain present and tested.
4. Automated source tests verify policy anchors plus version/changelog consistency; `bun run ci` exits 0.

## Constraints

1. Do not claim automatic native-edit interception or retry.
2. Do not route every small edit through Morph.
3. Keep Morph safety guards, path confinement, secret scrubbing, readonly protections, API request contract, and runtime behavior unchanged.
4. Do not create an npm release, alter unrelated OpenCode settings, or hand-edit deployed plugin files.
5. Do not create/push `v1.10.2` until Phase 9 proves the release commit reached the default branch.
6. Before changing `~/.config/opencode/package.json` or lock state, preserve non-secret current state in the configured dotfiles backup location and retain unrelated dependencies.

## Avoidances

1. Blind repetition of unchanged native edit input.
2. New plugin tool surface or runtime retry loop.
3. Weakening Morph API fallback or safety protections.
4. Creating a tag or GitHub release from an unmerged feature branch.
5. Updating only the installed package while leaving the configured stable instruction stale.

## Post-Archive Release Completion

These release-owned operations occur after user archive sign-off and successful ADV Phase 9 merge proof; they are not acceptance criteria for pre-merge source work.

- Create and push annotated tag `v1.10.2` at the merged default-branch commit.
- Confirm the tag-triggered GitHub workflow publishes non-draft release `v1.10.2` using the new changelog section.
- Pin the existing global OpenCode dependency to `github:JRedeker/opencode-morph-fast-apply#v1.10.2`, install it, and confirm the deployed package manifest reports `1.10.2`.
- Synchronize the separately configured stable instruction path from released package content.
- Run `opencode debug config`; report that OpenCode restart is required for plugin/instruction reload.

## Discovery Evidence

- Current source, installed package, latest tag, and latest GitHub release: `v1.10.1`.
- Tag release workflow runs on `v*`, tests/typechecks, and extracts notes from `CHANGELOG.md` section `## [version]`.
- Global OpenCode loads an installed plugin path and a separate stable instruction path.
- `adv-researcher` confirmed patch versioning, tag-after-merge, non-empty changelog, and deterministic Git-tag dependency pinning are appropriate; no contract-compromise risk remains under this release ordering.

## Sign-Off

User approved corrected release ordering in chat: “approve”.

# Design: v1.10.2 source preparation and post-archive release completion

## Pre-Merge Source Work

Keep existing native-edit recovery policy implementation unchanged. Add one release-preparation change set:

- `package.json`: version `1.10.2`.
- `README.md`: pinned plugin example `v1.10.2`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: non-empty `## [1.10.2]` section containing recovery-policy notes.
- `index.test.ts`: version/changelog consistency checks alongside existing policy coverage.
- `bun.lock`: regenerate only when package metadata requires it; frozen `bun ci` must pass.

The existing completed policy task maps only to SC1–SC3 and AC1–AC3. The new release-preparation task maps SC4–SC5 and AC4.

## Post-Archive Release Completion

After archive Phase 9 proves the release-preparation commit is reachable from default branch:

1. Verify the prospective tag target is an ancestor of `origin/trunk` with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
2. Create and push annotated tag `v1.10.2` at that merged commit.
3. Verify tag-triggered GitHub release publication and non-draft state.
4. Back up non-secret current OpenCode dependency/config state.
5. Pin only the existing global plugin dependency to `github:JRedeker/opencode-morph-fast-apply#v1.10.2`, install it, and verify installed manifest version.
6. Sync released packaged instruction to configured stable instruction path.
7. Run `opencode debug config`; require user restart for reload.

## Invariants

- Never tag or publish a feature-branch commit.
- Never hand-edit the deployed module.
- Never leave the separately configured stable instruction stale.
- Never claim source acceptance equals post-archive release completion.

## Validation

- Pre-merge: focused version/changelog tests and `bun run ci`.
- Post-archive: default-branch ancestry, GitHub release state, installed manifest version, instruction equivalence, and config diagnostic.

## Independent Validation

Independent researcher: applicable, high confidence, low risk. The corrected boundary eliminates orphan-tag risk from squash merges and leaves no contract-compromise risk.
